designSummary: Run chart of individual door-to-needle times, with the 2025 to 2026 baseline median as the centre line and standard run rules; an individuals chart to flag unusually long cases.
sampleSize: About 94 cases a year give roughly 45 to 50 cases in six months. With case-by-case plotting, a sustained 15-minute improvement is expected to trigger the shift rule within about 20 cases (c5), so a real change should be visible by the third cycle. The baseline uses the last 12 months of cases (about 94), which gives a stable median. Balancing measures are too rare for statistical comparison and are reviewed case by case.
primaryAnalysis: Run chart rules fixed in advance: a shift of six or more consecutive cases below the baseline median, a trend of five, too few or too many runs; cycle start dates marked on the chart.
secondaryAnalysis: Two-monthly proportion treated within 45 minutes; run charts of arrival-to-CT and CT-to-decision; counts of haemorrhage, treated mimics and delayed trauma scans with numerators and denominators.
missingData: Cases with missing step times stay on the primary chart; step charts show the number of cases with missing times.
multiplicity: One outcome measure carries the aim; the rest are descriptive.
software: Spreadsheet run chart template maintained by the stroke nurse.
overfittingGuards: Run rules and baseline fixed before cycle 1
No re-baselining until a sustained shift
Out-of-hours cases analysed within the same chart, marked, not removed
summary: Case-by-case run chart; a sustained 15-minute change expected to show within about 20 cases.
